solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Climate changes beginning to startle climber

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word climate are to be rearranged
beginning to points at only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A shift in the weather is starting to alarm a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer; it is a plant. CLIMATE rearranged gives CLEMATI, then S from 'startle'.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering vine is a classic garden plant that scrambles up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Cold old house right for group of statisticians

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: A chilly old building is fine for a team of number-crunchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Statisticians study a defined set of subjects sharing a characteristic, followed over time.

clue.text: Mission Spain oversaw gets in the way

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: gets in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
ran means managed or oversaw

explanation.surface: A Spanish operation's supervision is obstructive.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip or task one is sent on, a small mission.

clue.text: Dislike a pose adopted by actor Leonard

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into the actor's name

parts.note: Leonard Nimoy, the actor who played Spock
to sit is to pose for a portrait

explanation.surface: An actor disliked a certain posture.
explanation.definitionFit: This means hostility or ill will, a stronger form of dislike.

clue.text: Where to go for drinks and return as well

parts.note: into the bar is where one goes to get drinks
a return is a profit or gain

explanation.surface: A suggestion for where to drink and then come back too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means additionally, on top of everything else.

clue.text: Article penned by endlessly crafty hack

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within, as if in a pen
endlessly means the final letter of the word for crafty is dropped

parts.note: crafty means clever
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by a cunning journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist; here it is the verb to chop. 'endlessly' trims CLEVER to CLEVE, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack at something is to cut or split it roughly, a synonym.

clue.text: It can be hard to understand rambling old cops

definitions.text: It can be hard to understand

indicators.note: cops means catches or grabs, so the phrase holds the letters

explanation.surface: Some long-winded old police officers are difficult to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cops' looks like police; it is the verb to catch, holding the letters inside 'rambling old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon or a foreign tongue is speech that outsiders find hard to follow.

clue.text: A good sign: lots of social workers here

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A positive sign: plenty of care staff in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee colonies are kept in these places, and bees are social insects that work.

clue.text: Leave head early indicator of result?

parts.note: to exit is to leave
the poll is the head

explanation.surface: Telling someone to quit their top job prematurely.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey of voters leaving polling stations predicts an election outcome before the count.

clue.text: They run round the room avoiding the stage

parts.note: skirting means going round or avoiding
the boards means the theatre stage

explanation.surface: Actors racing about a room, keeping off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panels fixed along the foot of interior walls circle a room.

clue.text: Musician has time to go over price index

indicators.note: to go over means the outer letters cover the inner ones

parts.note: taken as written
RPI is the Retail Price Index, a British inflation measure

explanation.surface: A performer has to spend time reviewing an inflation figure.
explanation.walkthrough: RPI is the UK's Retail Price Index, a measure of inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the harp is one kind of musician.

clue.text: I think it's OK at sea without this raft

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the opening phrase are jumbled
without means the letters of the word this are subtracted from that pool

explanation.surface: Someone confidently claims they'll manage on the ocean with no raft.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: remove T, H, I, S from the letters of 'I think it's OK' and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor Heyerdahl's famous balsa vessel that crossed the Pacific in 1947 was a raft.

clue.text: Royal function involves performing music

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
on means on stage, performing
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A royal occasion includes a musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a musical form whose main theme keeps coming back, as in many concerto finales.

clue.text: In which to fly fish, not entirely upright

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the fish is left off

parts.note: a turbot is a flatfish
a prop is an upright support

explanation.surface: Advice on where to cast a fly for fish, while standing not quite straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly fish' suggests angling; 'fly' belongs to the definition. TURBOT shortened gives TURBO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a propeller aircraft driven by a gas turbine, something people travel in.

clue.text: Clock marksman in due course

parts.note: to clock a runner is to time them
Will Tell, short for William Tell, the legendary Swiss crossbow marksman

explanation.surface: Timing a sharpshooter, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' looks like a noun but is the verb to time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the truth will emerge eventually, given enough waiting.

clue.text: See raddled regent swigging first of tall glasses

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: swigging means drinking in, so the jumbled letters take another inside
raddled means worn out and disordered, rearranging the letters
first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Look at a dissolute ruler gulping from the first of some tall glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: REGENT rearranged with T taken in gives RGNETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spectacles held up on a long handle rather than worn.

clue.text: Barking hound implicated in comic mystery

indicators.note: implicated in means placed inside the comic

parts.note: a wit is a comic person

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of hound go wild

explanation.surface: A noisy dog is involved in a funny puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective story whose puzzle is the identity of the killer is a kind of mystery.

clue.text: Outrage troops breaching 3

indicators.note: breaching means breaking into the other piece

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer at 3 down, and enmity is a synonym of it
OR stands for other ranks, troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers breaking through, an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' sends you to 3 down; you use its synonym ENMITY.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means a grave crime or wickedness, an outrage.

clue.text: Love emblems incorporating rare animals

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like love

indicators.note: incorporating means the word for emblems takes another letter inside

parts.note: badges are emblems

explanation.surface: Romantic symbols featuring unusual creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: These fierce mustelids, also called ratels, are African and Asian mammals.

clue.text: Where staff, say, get introduction to equines

definitions.text: Where staff, say, get introduction to equines

parts.note: to man is to staff
eg means for example, say

indicators.note: introduction to means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A place where workers are first introduced to horses.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a riding school where horses and riders are trained.

clue.text: Strike American defending a gap

indicators.note: defending means surrounding and protecting the letter

parts.note: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A US striker protecting a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or break in continuity, a gap.

clue.text: Died ordering different bottle

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

indicators.note: different means the letters of ordering come out in another form

explanation.surface: Someone passed away after asking for another wine bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a container; it is British slang for nerve or courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang means courage, and this phrase means heroic daring.

clue.text: Irish love importing fine timber

indicators.note: importing means bringing in another piece

parts.note: love in tennis is zero, O
OK means fine

explanation.surface: An Irish lover bringing in fine timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardwood from tropical Africa used in furniture and boat building is a timber.

clue.text: One admirer returns carrying a canteen

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed pair holds another letter
returns means the pieces for one and admirer are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A fan comes back with a water flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns I + FAN into NAFI, which holds A. The NAAFI runs shops and canteens for British service personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes is the British military's catering and shop organisation.

clue.text: Healthy bird's last to head for capital

indicators.note: last to head means the final letter of the bird is moved to the front

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or healthy, written AI
a robin is a bird; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A fit bird is the last one to set off for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: AI (A1) plus ROBIN; 'last to head' carries ROBIN's N to the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: Pair of soaks hire a sanctuary

indicators.note: hire means take on, so the doubled word takes on a letter
pair of means the word for soaks appears twice

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it to soften the fibres

explanation.surface: Two drunks hire a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaks' looks like drunkards; it is the verb RET, used twice, and 'hire' (take on) puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet refuge, a synonym of a safe haven.

clue.text: Escort model over visiting Times

parts.note: a toy is a model, as a toy car

indicators.note: visiting means one piece goes into another

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An escort and a model are featured in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is BY, as in 3 by 4.
explanation.definitionFit: A young man who is the lover or companion of an older woman can act as her escort.

clue.text: School tests quantities of arsenic

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
levels are amounts or quantities

explanation.surface: Pupils are tested for amounts of poison.
explanation.walkthrough: AS levels are British school exams taken at about age 17.
explanation.definitionFit: These are British exams sat in the sixth form, below full A levels.
